transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-07-07
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sam Brooks (NovaRetail - Head of ML), Maya Li (NovaRetail - Platform Eng), Jordan Park (NovaRetail - CTO)
Recording: auto

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on model selection, version pinning strategy, and validating rollback/fallback behavior. Reviewed last week's benchmark results, discussed regression observed on v1.3 for short-context prompts, and agreed on tests for rollback and canary rollout. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Topics Covered:
- Recap of benchmarks (latency, accuracy, cost)
- Pinning strategy: when to pin, how to pin to major/minor versions
- Rollback/fallback flows and canary tests
- Catalog comparison: Redwood catalog variants (quantized, fp16, trimmed seq) vs external models
- Data sharing & evaluation criteria for production readiness

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um it's Alex from Redwood, I'll kick us off. 
00:06 Priya Kapoor: Hi all, Priya here, I'll cover the technical bits on pinning and rollback. 
00:12 Sam Brooks: Morning, yeah thanks. We had time to run those tests you shared, there are a few oddities on the short prompts. 
00:20 Alex Chen: Cool. Quick agenda, recap benchmarks, discuss pinning strategy, then plan a rollback test, ok? 
00:27 Jordan Park: Fine by me. We're watching latency and token cost closely, our SREs flagged a 12% token increase on v1.3 for the checkout flow. 
00:36 Maya Li: For clarity the increase is tokens-per-prompt not raw latency; the cost delta matters to our finance folks. 
00:44 Priya Kapoor: Right, and the team saw that too — v1.3 has a different tokenizer behavior in some edge prompts, so tokens expand on short, templated prompts. We're seeing it in the eval set you gave. 
00:57 Sam Brooks: Ok that's consistent. We also saw a slight drop in rerank accuracy on a subset of out-of-distribution SKUs, like newer product descriptions. 
01:06 Alex Chen: Thanks for flagging. So there are two levers: pin the model to a previous vetted version for critical routes, and/or implement a fallback to a smaller or quantized variant if latency or token count breaches a threshold. 
01:18 Priya Kapoor: Right. Quick note on pinning semantics in Redwood: you can pin to a specific model artifact (e.g., redwood-v1.2.fp16) or to a named channel like "stable". Pinning to artifact gives deterministic outputs; channel pins can drift. 
01:33 Sam Brooks: We want deterministic outputs for checkout suggestions — any change that modifies tokenization or answer shape could break downstream ranking. 
01:41 Priya Kapoor: Then artifact-level pinning is the recommendation. For your POC, I'd suggest pinning checkout route to redwood-v1.2.fp16 and non-critical routes to redwood-v1.3-quantized for cost savings. 
01:52 Maya Li: How do rollbacks work operationally? If we detect regression, can we flip back instantly? 
02:00 Priya Kapoor: Yes. We have canary policies: rollout to 5% of traffic, monitor latency, token delta, and quality metrics. If any SLOs breach, you can trigger automated rollback to the pinned artifact or to a fallback family. The control plane also keeps the previous artifact ready for instant activation. 
02:17 Jordan Park: What's the expected failover window? We need to tell SREs what to expect. 
02:21 Priya Kapoor: In practice the control plane switch is subsecond for routing, but ongoing in-flight requests will finish on the old model. For effective mitigation, we recommend draining with a 30–60s window; our telemetry will show traffic switchover. 
02:37 Sam Brooks: Sounds good. Can we test that now? Run a rollback drill with a small synthetic workload? 
02:42 Alex Chen: We planned that. Priya, can you run the rollback test on staging and share logs? 
02:46 Priya Kapoor: Yep, I'll schedule the test — plan: deploy v1.3 to canary at 5%, then force a regression flag and roll back to v1.2, capture latency/token metrics and explainability logs. We will include KV cache hit rates too because prefix caching affected some of your longer sessions. 
03:01 Maya Li: Good. Also, about catalog comparisons, you mentioned quantized variants — are those lossful in ways that would impact rerank quality? 
03:09 Priya Kapoor: Some small delta. The Optimize team ran MRR and BLEU-like evals; for most retail prompts quantized 4-bit variants have <1.5% MRR delta but 2–4x throughput improvement and lower cost. For NovaRetail's skewed SKU descriptions, we should run the same evals on your sample set to confirm. 
03:28 Sam Brooks: We'll provide a 2k prompt sample set. Expecting results by next sync. 
03:33 Alex Chen: Please attach the spreadsheet with cost calc; the last one we sent had cost per 1M tokens for fp16 vs 4-bit quantized. 
03:41 Sam Brooks: Got it. One more thing: tokenization differences — can you map which prompts expand tokens on v1.3? That'll help our engineers mitigate. 
03:49 Priya Kapoor: We can produce a delta report that lists top 50 prompts with token delta and suggested prompt normalizations. We'll also show the tokenizer config change that likely caused it. 
03:58 Jordan Park: On security, if we do a canary with hosted in our VPC, are there any extra steps? We are leaning towards private deployment eventually. 
04:07 Alex Chen: For POC, hosted with VPC peering is fine; Redwood Private is available but requires procurement cycles. For canary we'll use TLS+KMS-managed keys; access logs can be exported to your S3 for audit. 
04:21 Maya Li: Perfect. Can you share the security checklist again? 
04:25 Alex Chen: Yes, I'll reshare SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML config, and the KMS integration checklist after the call. 
04:33 Sam Brooks: Great. Back to pinning policy — do we want automatic roll-forward on patch releases? We prefer ops to approve roll-forwards. 
04:41 Priya Kapoor: There are two modes: automatic minor patch adoption or manual. For ops-sensitive routes you can set manual approval and require a canary pass. We'll document the recommended guardrails. 
04:51 Alex Chen: OK let's recap action items and next steps. Priya will run rollback test and send logs. Alex will send updated benchmark spreadsheet and pinned-model matrix. Maya will share production-like prompt samples and S3 location for logs. We'll tentatively schedule a canary rollout for next week subject to results. 
05:08 Sam Brooks: That's accurate. Any blockers from Redwood side? 
05:12 Priya Kapoor: Nothing blocking; we just need the sample prompts and a time window for the rollback test. 
05:18 Jordan Park: Alright, thanks everyone. 
05:20 Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the spreadsheet.
